rationale: D1, data-informed (not zero-shot): the first candidate of the front model. A flame on a thin fuel in concurrent flow is a band: a front that advances at a rate linear in flow and rising with oxygen, a visible tip ahead of it by an overhang that follows the flow within seconds, and a base that repeats the front one burn-through time later. The three tracked train burns give the rate at four flows and two oxygen levels, the overhang from three fan steps and the burn-through time; the published theory gives the functional forms and the quench boundary, moved to where the one train burn that never spread puts it. Every number typed by the author; no fit, no search; the validation burns were measured by other agents into files the author has not opened.
